  The commits you're remembering (June 28, a trio landed in sequence):
  - d52881ea2 — palm fronds slimmed 80B→24B + their own GPU buffer (req_2016)

  fix didn't get bypassed.

  What's actually biting you is a different animal: hard preview budgets. That commit allocates each family's buffer once, cap-sized, in world_loader.zig:79-83: grass 65,536 · bush 16,384 · flower 16,384 · fronds 24,576 · trunks 2,048. When a family hits its cap, pushFoliageRow just
  returns false and rows drop. Your topless trees are arithmetic: one palm is one trunk row but a whole crown of frond rows, so the frond budget exhausts long before the trunk budget — trunks keep placing, tops silently stop.

  Why only the iso editor: this is by design a preview path — the comment in the code literally says "the Compile bake grows the full population." The compiled world streams chunks with view-distance and LOD so no single buffer ever holds everything; the paint preview is one flat
  cap-sized buffer for the entire painted field. The only warning when it fills is a stderr log line ([paint] LIVE FOLIAGE PREVIEW FULL …) that you'd never see in the UI — which violates your standing juice-limits ruling twice over: the cap is set low and the truncation is silent
  where you're looking.

  So for the shit list: the ask isn't "re-fix memory," it's raise/rethink the preview budgets (at 24B a frond, 10× the frond cap is ~6MB — cheap) and make the truncation loud in the viewport, or make the preview regenerate view-scoped like the streamer instead of whole-field. Logged
  all of this on the board with the commit shas so the world session inherits it grounded.

events.text: GAP TT — topless trees in the 3D iso painter are NOT a memory-footprint regression; the slim pipeline is intact. Confirmed from req_2648 (origin thread) and re-grounded in current source. Root cause = hard LIVE-FOLIAGE PREVIEW budgets in world_loader.zig:79-83 (grass 65536 / bush 16384 / flower 16384 / frond 24576 / trunk 2048). Per palm (spec 3, world_loader.zig:7188-7199) ONE trunk row goes to the trunk buffer, then crown.total() FROND rows go to the frond buffer. Frond cap (24576) exhausts at ~1500 palms (~16 fronds each) while the trunk cap (2048) still has headroom -> palms keep getting trunks after fronds stop -> topless palms. pushFoliageRow (7121) returns false and drops the row; the ONLY signal is a stderr log.print at 7225-7228 ('[paint] LIVE FOLIAGE PREVIEW FULL ...'), invisible in the viewport. Violates juice-limits ruling twice: cap set low + silent truncation where the user is looking. Why iso-editor-only: deliberate flat preview path (one cap-sized buffer for the whole painted field); the Compile bake + compiled streamer grow the full population view-scoped/LOD. Fix direction (deferred until greenlight): raise caps (10x fronds @ ~24B/row ~6MB, cheap), OR surface truncation loudly in viewport, OR regenerate preview view-scoped like the streamer. Slim commits: d52881ea2 (fronds req_2016), d990ee74f (grass/bush/flower req_2019), dc2b02dcc (universal instance req_2036).

FIX LANDED (agent, commit 612267e4b): preview caps raised — grass 262144, bush 65536, flower 65536, frond 262144, trunk 16384 (frond:trunk exactly 16:1 matching one palm = 1 trunk + ~16 fronds; old ratio was 12:1, the topless-tree arithmetic). Saturation log now marks WHICH family CLIPPED. ast-check + ship clean. Visual proof deferred to the user's next forest-paint. WATCH-ITEM flagged by the agent, not a bug today: static slim-instance retention reserves the cap-sized slice, so a fully-warmed paint preview holds 655360/1048576 rows (62.5%) of the shared slim pool (framework/gpu/3d.zig:3868 MAX_STATIC_INSTANCES); latecomer baked-world slim batches past ~393k rows degrade to the per-frame dynamic path (3d.zig:6689), not dropped. If slim-pool contention ever shows, MAX_STATIC_INSTANCES is the lever.
